engine: The PURE numeral ODOMETER-ROLL mechanic, EXTRACTED out of stat-odometer's own pinned ScrollTrigger so other atoms can borrow the roll WITHOUT importing stat-odometer's pin (resolves a pin-budget conflict: stat-odometer owns_pin AND minutes-bloom owns_pin). A vertical strip of numbers (.nor-num, one per value) sits inside a one-number-tall overflow:hidden window; the column (.nor-col) is translated on Y so the active value sits in the window: translateY = -(index + f) * rowHeight. The number ROLLS — the old slides up and out, the new rolls up from below. Pure transform; the window clips the rest.

measured_teardown.move: extracted verbatim from stat-odometer S11 (component.js lines 88-92 build the column, 146-150 drive the roll: numWrap.style.transform = 'translateY(' + (-(i + f) * h) + 'px)'). Here that translate is split off the pin into two PURE drivers: set(p 0..1) maps a host's progress across the whole value sequence (fpos = p*(N-1)) every frame; to(n) tweens the same translateY to a new value (a visible roll, GSAP power3.out-class, or a snap under reduced-motion / no-GSAP). owns_pin:false — NO ScrollTrigger of its own.
measured_teardown.cited: stat-odometer / Springs '3 / 9 / 10 / 16' pinned stat-card: the giant serif number changes via an ODOMETER ROLL (old digit translates up and out, new rolls up from below) — that numeral column, on its own, pin-less.

values.what: the value sequence the column rolls through (e.g. [9,10,6] — minutes to places). Omit to read from .nor-num markup, or pass a single value.

value.what: the starting value (matched within values; else the first row). to(n) and set(p) move from here.

digits.what: pad each value to this many characters with a leading thin-space so a 1-digit and a 2-digit number share a steady tabular band (9 vs 10).

ease.what: tween ease for to(); token -> gsap ease (air=power3.out, glide=power2.out, linear=none, snap=expo.out). Pass a raw gsap ease string too. set(p) is linear (tracks the host 1:1).

dur.what: tween seconds for to(). set(p) has no duration (frame-driven).

entry: NumeralOdometerRoll.create(target, opts) -> { to(n), set(p), value, index, reflow(), destroy }. target = a .nor-window (or any el) containing .nor-col. set(p 0..1) is a PURE pin-driver across the value sequence; to(n) animates to a value. owns_pin false.
law: translateY (the column) only; the window is overflow:hidden (clips the rest); GPU layer; tabular-nums so digits roll as a steady band; NO mix-blend / NO backdrop / NO WebGL / NO width/height/top/left animation. reduced-motion -> to() snaps (no tween). owns_pin:false — NO ScrollTrigger of its own; a host pin/scrub drives set(p). will-change cleared after each to() one-shot.
gate_mode: drive set(p) 0..1 across [9,10,6] OR call to(10) then to(6): the active number sits in a one-number-tall window and visibly ROLLS (old slides up/out, new rolls up). Verify the window CLIPS (overflow hidden — only one number shows), the roll is translateY-only, and there is NO ScrollTrigger inside this atom. Distinct from stat-odometer (that owns the pin + bg/photo/label choreography; this is JUST the numeral column, pin-less).
proven: lab: a big serif minute number rolling 9 -> 10 -> 6 (minutes to real Агрономічне places), driven both by to(n) buttons AND by a synthetic set(p) sweep (no ScrollTrigger). Window clips to one number; column translateY = -(i+f)*rowHeight; tabular band steady across 1- and 2-digit values.
